players.product: 8-inch and 12-inch specialty foundry: power discretes (super-junction MOSFET, IGBT), embedded and standalone non-volatile memory, analog and power management, logic and RF

quarterly_data.signal: EVP and CFO Daniel Wang: Q2 2026 revenue reached an all-time high of $717.5 million, up 26.8% year on year and 8.6% on Q1, on higher wafer shipments and ASP. By region, China revenue was $563.7 million (78.6% of the total, +20%, on MCU, flash, Trench MOSFET, logic and smart card ICs), North America $93.8 million (+77%, power management IC and MCU), other Asia $32 million (+11.6%) and Europe $28 million (+90.1%, MCU and smart card ICs). Operating cash flow was $330.1 million and cash $4.53 billion at June 30. Chairman and President Dr. Peng Bai: much of the North America revenue is BCD PMIC for AI server boxes, and Europe grows as large European companies pursue a China-for-China strategy with Hua Hong as a partner.

Chairman and President Dr. Peng Bai: on some products Hua Hong 'clearly cannot meet the demand'; the orders it receives are 'anywhere between 1.5x-2x of our capacity' while its fabs are 'pretty much 100% loaded'. Supply has tightened since the start of the year, driving price increases mostly in MCU, memory and PMIC; he expects price increases to continue through H2 2026 and perhaps into 2027, in percentage terms rather than DRAM-like multiples, and Hua Hong uses pricing and capacity fungibility between platforms to match demand to capacity. EVP and CFO Daniel Wang: roughly 60% of the guided Q3 revenue increase comes from ASP and 40% from volume, led by MCU / embedded memory (double-digit growth), standalone memory, low- and medium-voltage MOSFETs, RF and PMIC / analog, while IGBT and super junction are virtually flat.

Chairman and President Dr. Peng Bai: Fab 9A in Wuxi has all its equipment installed and reaches total capacity in Q3, loaded 100% from Q3, with a full fab's output in 2027; the next fab, Fab 9B, under construction since March, starts equipment installation in Q3, should have a completed line in Q1 with small volume, and ramps through 2027. EVP and CFO Daniel Wang: this third 12-inch fab ramps over the next three years to 55,000 wafers of capacity for approximately $6 billion of capex, roughly $2 billion a year (Dr. Bai: less than $2 billion a year, $1.5 billion). Dr. Bai: the final step of the Huali Microelectronics acquisition should take place within about a month, after which its results are consolidated from Q3; capacity will go mainly to MCU (moving from 55 nanometers to 40 nanometers), BCD and NOR flash.
quarterly_data.figure: third 12-inch fab: 55,000 wafers capacity, approximately $6 billion capex

quarterly_data.signal: EVP and CFO Daniel Wang: H2 2026 depreciation is projected at about $55 million for the 8-inch business, around $250 million for the first 12-inch fab, roughly $210 million for the second and about $30 million for Huali Microelectronics ($50 million-$60 million a year and declining); the $25.4 million government equipment grant received in Q2 was for Shanghai, and the Wuxi part will most likely be paid in Q4 2026. Chairman and President Dr. Peng Bai: equipment lead times are increasing but manageable since much equipment was booked last year, newer fabs will use a higher share of domestic equipment, and helium spiked temporarily because of the Middle East war before easing.

Chairman and President Dr. Peng Bai: some of Hua Hong's MCUs already go into silicon photonics optical modules, and it plans, at an early stage, to expand into more silicon-based ICs inside those modules; it is also planning a more complete power-device offering as silicon carbide enters power modules. He sees demand strong in H2 2026 and, by consensus, 2027, with 2028 debated; industry closures of 8-inch fabs benefit Hua Hong's three 8-inch fabs. Consumer-market weakness has had little visible impact at the foundry level, and memory makers may in time move peripheral logic dies to larger foundries.
